option_a: Cue: send any grid card to the discard and gain one Ticket Stub
option_b: Cue: send any grid card to the discard and gain Ticket Stubs equal to its rank
option_c: Cue: send any grid card to the discard for one Ticket Stub, or destroy it outright for three

name: The Shredder
one_line_summary: Worth more destroyed than sold
option_a: Destroys itself when sold and pays double its price
option_b: Destroys itself when sold and pays double, and cannot be sold at all in the first three towns
option_c: Destroys itself when sold and pays triple, but selling it also removes one other card

name: Astronomer
one_line_summary: One category is free
option_a: All cards of one named category are free in the shop
option_b: All cards of one named category are free in the shop, and the category changes each town
option_c: One card per shop is free, and you choose which

name: Common
one_line_summary: While in the deck, doubles the odds of Rare cards appearing in packs and shops
option_a: While in the deck, doubles the chance of Rare cards appearing in packs and shops
option_b: While in the deck, doubles the chance of the rarity one step above this card's own appearing
option_c: While on the grid, the next pack opened contains one guaranteed Rare

name: Canfield rules economy
one_line_summary: Pay in cards, get paid in gold
option_a: Economy variant: you pay cards to play and earn gold per card scored
option_b: Economy variant: you pay cards to play and earn gold per line scored rather than per card
option_c: Economy variant: you pay one card per act and earn gold equal to that act's combo

name: Card-stack shop pricing
one_line_summary: Buying is also thinning
option_a: Shop prices are paid as a stack of cards drawn from your own deck to match the listed value, so buying thins the deck
option_b: Shop prices are paid as a stack of cards you choose from your deck to match the listed value
option_c: Shop prices may be paid in gold or in cards, at a better rate in cards

name: Cards as currency
one_line_summary: No money, only cards
option_a: Cards are the only currency; there is no gold at all
option_b: Cards are the only currency, and a card's trade value is its rank
option_c: Cards are the only currency, and their trade value is set by rarity rather than rank

name: Mana cards
one_line_summary: Any card is fuel
option_a: Any card may be spent as a resource instead of played, with no separate resource bar
option_b: Any card may be spent as a resource; its value is its rank
option_c: Any card may be spent as a resource, and spending one from the Entrance costs no act

name: Heat as second currency
one_line_summary: Heat, earned by being the villain
option_a: Heel shows earn heat instead of fame, and some towns pay more for a villain
option_b: Heel shows earn heat alongside fame, and heat buys different things than fame does
option_c: Heel shows earn heat instead of fame; heat cannot buy cards but can buy rule changes

name: Masked satire (Talchum)
one_line_summary: The mask takes the anger
option_a: Earns heat safely: while masked, the town's retaliation lands on the mask rather than the card
option_b: Earns heat safely while masked, and the mask breaks after three shows
option_c: Earns heat safely while masked; unmasking converts all accumulated heat into fame at once

name: The Cheap Pop
one_line_summary: When scored, grants a small bonus fame in every town
option_a: When scored, grants a small amount of bonus fame in every town
option_b: When scored, grants bonus fame scaling with how many shows you have already played in this town
option_c: When scored, grants bonus fame, doubled in any town you have never performed in before

name: Credit Card
one_line_summary: Lets you go into debt
option_a: You may spend into debt down to a fixed negative limit
option_b: You may spend into debt with no limit, but shows pay out to the debt first
option_c: You may spend into debt down to a limit, and interest accrues on what you owe

name: Cube
one_line_summary: Cheap because it costs you
option_a: A flat bonus, and acquiring it puts you into debt
option_b: A flat bonus, and holding it costs gold every show
option_c: A large flat bonus that puts you into debt, and the debt must be cleared before the run can be won

name: Luxury Tax
one_line_summary: Wealth costs you room
option_a: The Entrance shrinks by one card for every fixed amount of gold you hold
option_b: The Entrance shrinks by one for every fixed amount of gold held, down to a floor of two
option_c: The grid loses one usable cell for every fixed amount of gold held

name: Rich get Richer
one_line_summary: You cannot score more than you own
option_a: Points scored are capped at your current gold
option_b: Points scored are capped at your current gold, and exceeding the cap converts the excess to gold at a poor rate
option_c: Points scored are capped at your gold, and gold is capped at your fame

name: The Claque
one_line_summary: Consumable: raises this show's fame floor to 60% of goal, but costs 1 Gold at every subsequent show forever
option_a: Consumable: this show's floor rises to 60% of goal, but every later show costs 1 gold, forever
option_b: Consumable: this show's floor rises to 60% of goal, and the next three shows each cost 1 gold
option_c: Consumable: this show's floor rises to 60% of goal, and every later show's reward drops by 5%

name: The Greed
one_line_summary: Being rich raises the bar
option_a: Boss: the goal rises with the gold you hold when the show is selected
option_b: Boss: the goal rises with the gold you hold, recalculated at every act
option_c: Boss: the goal rises with gold held, and spending gold mid-show lowers it again

name: The Ox
one_line_summary: Boss: your favourite hand costs you everything
option_a: Boss: scoring your most-played hand type sets your gold to nothing
option_b: Boss: scoring your most-played hand type halves your gold each time
option_c: Boss: scoring your most-played hand type costs gold equal to what that line scored

name: Inflation
one_line_summary: Everything you buy raises the prices
option_a: Every purchase permanently raises all shop prices
option_b: Every purchase permanently raises all shop prices, and every sale lowers them
option_c: Every purchase raises prices for the rest of the town only

name: Rotten Egg
one_line_summary: Crashes the sale price of everything
option_a: Sets the sell value of every card, present and future, to the minimum, then destroys itself once it has earned enough
option_b: Sets the sell value of every card to the minimum permanently, with no escape
option_c: Halves the sell value of every card, and pays you the difference each time one is sold

name: Banner
one_line_summary: Paid for the discards you did not use
option_a: Scores bonus points per unused Entrance discard remaining
option_b: Scores bonus points per unused discard, doubled if none were used at all
option_c: Scores bonus points per unused discard and per unused undo, together

name: Crazy Tan escalating draw penalty
one_line_summary: Skipping compounds
option_a: Each consecutive turn without a legal placement raises the number of cards the next player must discard by one
option_b: Each consecutive turn without a legal placement discards one extra card from the deck, resetting when a placement happens
option_c: Each turn without a placement raises the discard penalty by one and lowers the show's goal by the same

name: Delayed Gratification
one_line_summary: Paid for restraint
option_a: Earn gold per discard if no discards were used by the end of the show
option_b: Earn gold per unused discard, whether or not any were used
option_c: Earn gold per unused discard, and the rate rises the longer you go without using one

name: Green Joker
one_line_summary: Rises with acts, falls with discards
option_a: Gains a multiplier per act played this show and loses one per discard used
option_b: Gains a multiplier per act played this show, with discards costing nothing
option_c: Gains a multiplier per act played and loses two per discard, so the choice is sharp

name: The Loose Card
one_line_summary: Discard whatever is connected to nothing. (line 845)
option_a: Any card with no connection to anything else in its column may be discarded freely, and the column closes up behind it
option_b: Any card with no connection to anything else in its column may be discarded freely, and a replacement is drawn onto that column
option_c: Any card that is part of no potential meld at all may be discarded freely, whatever its column

name: The Mulligan
one_line_summary: Throws one card back
option_a: Discard one Entrance card per turn before placement; further copies add one discard each
option_b: Discard any number of Entrance cards per turn, but each discard after the first costs 1 gold
option_c: Discard one Entrance card per turn, and the discarded card is replaced immediately from the deck

name: Fame banks at Continue
one_line_summary: A win is not banked until you say so
option_a: Fame is committed only when you press Continue after a win, so the show stays undoable until then
option_b: Fame is committed at the outcome screen, and only the last act is undoable
option_c: Fame is committed when you press Continue, and you may replay the show once instead of banking it

name: Free Undo
one_line_summary: Grants one free undo per turn that does not carry over
option_a: One free undo per turn, which does not carry over
option_b: One free undo per turn, and unused undos accumulate up to three
option_c: Unlimited undos until the first line scores each show, and none after

name: The Escapologist
one_line_summary: Free undo becomes 2 per turn, and all debuffs on your cards expire one show sooner
option_a: Free undos become two per turn, and debuffs on your cards expire one show sooner
option_b: Free undos become two per turn
option_c: Free undos become two per turn, and an undo also rewinds any debuff applied since

name: Live undo during resolution
one_line_summary: Undo mid-resolution
option_a: Pressing Undo during a resolving act cancels it: resolution fast-forwards and the pre-act board returns, costing no act
option_b: Pressing Undo during a resolving act cancels it, but the act is still spent
option_c: Pressing Undo during a resolving act pauses it, letting you resume or cancel after seeing what has resolved so far

name: The Ledger of Undos
one_line_summary: Undo accrual has to account for its own rewinding. (line 807)
option_a: Undos accrue every few turns; undoing rewinds the turn counter, and the game tracks what you already banked so a rewind cannot mint you a second one
option_b: Undos accrue every few turns, and rewinding past the point one was earned takes it back again
option_c: Undos accrue per turn and are banked permanently the moment they are earned, so rewinding never touches them

name: The Rewinder
one_line_summary: Spends your safety net for points
option_a: Cue: destroy your oldest undo snapshots for bonus points each, up to five per act
option_b: Cue: destroy every undo snapshot you hold for bonus points each, once per show
option_c: Cue: destroy your oldest undo snapshot for bonus points scaling with how many turns ago it was taken

name: Escalating reroll cost
one_line_summary: Rerolling gets dearer
option_a: Shop reroll cost rises with each use within a shop
option_b: Shop reroll cost rises with each use and does not reset between shops
option_c: Shop reroll cost rises with each use, and the first reroll of each shop is always free

name: Flash Card
one_line_summary: Grows on rerolls
option_a: Gains a permanent bonus for every shop reroll you make
option_b: Gains a permanent bonus per reroll, and the reroll cost stops rising while it is held
option_c: Gains a permanent bonus per reroll, and loses one for each shop you leave without rerolling

name: Burglar
one_line_summary: More acts, no discards
option_a: When a show begins, gain extra acts and lose every discard for that show
option_b: When a show begins, gain extra acts and lose every discard and undo
option_c: You choose at show start how many discards to trade for how many extra acts

name: John Robinson
one_line_summary: Elite hazard: the show is shortened to 2 submits instead of 3, with the goal unchanged
option_a: Elite hazard: the show has 2 submits instead of 3, with the goal unchanged
option_b: Elite hazard: the show has 2 submits instead of 3, and the goal drops 20%
option_c: Elite hazard: the show ends the moment any grid is completely filled

name: The All-Nighter
one_line_summary: Three times the show
option_a: Show: triple the submits, triple the goal, triple the reward
option_b: Show: triple the submits and goal, with the reward scaling to how far past the goal you get
option_c: Show: triple the submits and goal, and the deck is not reshuffled between them

name: The Needle
one_line_summary: Boss: one act only
option_a: Boss: the show has a single act, at a proportionally lower goal
option_b: Boss: the show has a single act at the full goal
option_c: Boss: the show has a single act, and every line completed in it scores twice

name: Audience Patience
one_line_summary: Each show, patience starts at N; each pickup or placement spends 1 patience, a unique effect trigger refunds 1; at 0 patience the Entrance auto-commits
option_a: Patience starts at 20 each show; every pickup or placement spends 1 and every unique effect trigger refunds 1; at 0 the Entrance auto-commits its remaining cards to random cells
option_b: Patience starts at 20 each show and is spent only by placement, never by pickup; at 0 the show ends immediately and scores what is on the grid
option_c: Each grid carries its own patience of 10; running one grid dry locks it and forces the Entrance onto another grid

name: Lavender Loop
one_line_summary: The goal grows while you think
option_a: The show's goal rises steadily with real time spent in it
option_b: The show's goal rises with the number of actions taken, not with real time
option_c: The show's goal rises with real time, and pausing stops the clock at a fame cost

name: Roman Numerals rank
one_line_summary: A rank that keeps time
option_a: Ranks run 1 to 12 and wrap; the rank advances by 1 with every player action
option_b: Ranks run 1 to 12 and wrap; the rank advances by 1 with every line completed
option_c: Ranks run 1 to 12 and wrap; the rank advances by 1 per action, and you may cue to stop the clock for a turn

name: The Charivari
one_line_summary: If 4 or more cards are placed onto the grid on the first turn of a show, gain bonus multiplier on the first act's payout
option_a: If four or more cards are placed on the first turn of a show, the first act's payout gains a multiplier
option_b: If the whole Entrance is placed within one turn, that act's payout gains a multiplier
option_c: Each act gains a multiplier scaling with how few turns it took to fill the lines that scored in it

name: La Belle Lucie merci rule
one_line_summary: One mercy move
option_a: When no legal moves remain, one card may be shifted up or down by one position
option_b: When no legal moves remain, one card may be moved anywhere, once per show
option_c: One mercy move is granted per show whether or not you are stuck, and it is lost if unused

name: Soundcheck
one_line_summary: At show start, grants one free move (grab and place one stack) before the first Entrance refresh, without spending an act
option_a: At show start, one free grab-and-place before the first Entrance refresh, costing no act
option_b: At the start of every act, one free grab-and-place costing no act
option_c: At show start, one free grab-and-place, and another every time a grid is completely filled

name: Stuntman
one_line_summary: Huge, and it costs you room
option_a: A very large flat bonus, at the cost of two Entrance slots
option_b: A very large flat bonus, at the cost of one act per show
option_c: A very large flat bonus, at the cost of two Entrance slots, refundable by selling it

name: 5D multiverse time-travel card
one_line_summary: Sends a card into the past
option_a: Cue: send a card into a past board state, play that board out, and keep only what differs from the present
option_b: Cue: send a card into the previous turn's board state and replay that turn with it there
option_c: Cue: rewind the grid to its state three turns ago, keeping every card you have gained since

name: Labyrinth
one_line_summary: Every act is the first act
option_a: Every act counts as the first act of the show for every effect that cares
option_b: Every act counts as the first act, and every discard as the first discard
option_c: Every act counts as the first, and every act also counts as the last

name: The Crowd Takes Over
one_line_summary: The audience plays your turn
option_a: For one turn, a seeded random audience makes your moves for you
option_b: For one turn the audience makes your moves, and anything it scores pays double
option_c: For one turn the audience proposes each move and you may veto one of them

name: The Fourth Wall
one_line_summary: Once per act, during scoring resolution, pauses the show to allow one grab/place before resolution continues
option_a: Once per act, pause scoring mid-resolution to make one grab and place before resolution continues
option_b: Once per show, pause scoring mid-resolution to make one grab and place
option_c: Once per act, pause scoring mid-resolution to make one grab and place, but the paused line scores at half

name: The Time Signature
one_line_summary: Splits the submit in two
option_a: Rows score at Submit as normal; columns score at the start of the next turn against the board as it then stands, and the combo carries across
option_b: Rows score at Submit; columns score at the start of the next turn, and the combo resets between them
option_c: You choose per act whether rows or columns resolve first, and the second one resolves against the board the first one left

name: Paper the House
one_line_summary: Consumable: auto-passes one town's fame check, but grants zero fame and zero rewards from it
option_a: Consumable: one town's requirement passes automatically, granting no fame and no rewards
option_b: Consumable: one town's requirement passes automatically at half fame and half rewards
option_c: Consumable: one town's requirement passes automatically, and the following town's goal rises by the fame you skipped

name: Golden Buzzer
one_line_summary: Consumable, once per run: skips one town's requirement entirely for an instant win with full rewards
option_a: Consumable, once per run: one show is skipped and counts as won with full rewards
option_b: Consumable, once per run: one show is skipped and counts as won, with no rewards
option_c: Consumable, once per run: one show is won immediately at whatever score is already on the grid

name: The Gong
one_line_summary: Town hazard: any submit scoring under 25% of goal ends the show immediately
option_a: Town hazard: any submit scoring under 25% of goal ends the show at once
option_b: Town hazard: any submit scoring under 25% of goal costs you an act
option_c: Town hazard: any submit scoring less than the one before it ends the show at once

name: The Big Top
one_line_summary: Priced in board space
option_a: This card blocks the four cells around it, which can never be filled, and scores hugely for it
option_b: This card blocks the four cells around it, and scores in proportion to how many it is blocking
option_c: This card blocks its neighbours until it scores, then releases them

name: The Clearance
one_line_summary: Room is the resource
option_a: Rule: effects are paid for with empty cells rather than gold, at a fixed rate
option_b: Rule: effects may be paid for with empty cells or gold, your choice, at a fixed rate
option_c: Rule: effects are paid for with empty cells, and a full grid means nothing can fire

name: The Deposit
one_line_summary: Pay a cell to fire
option_a: Cue: permanently destroy one empty cell on the grid to fire this card's effect
option_b: Cue: block one empty cell for the rest of the show to fire this card's effect
option_c: Cue: block one empty cell per use, so repeated use costs more and more room

name: The Casting Call
one_line_summary: Lets you choose the target every time
option_a: Each time this card triggers, you choose which card its effect lands on
option_b: Each time this card triggers, you choose the target from three the card offers
option_c: Each time this card triggers you choose the target, and choosing the same one twice running doubles it

name: The Director's Note
one_line_summary: Fires, then asks
option_a: When a line scores, choose which of its cards keeps the bonus for the rest of the show
option_b: When a line scores, choose one of its cards to score again immediately
option_c: When a line scores, choose between a large bonus now and a smaller permanent one

name: The Fork
one_line_summary: Two roads, pick one
option_a: Consumable: offers two effects drawn at random; you take one and the other is lost
option_b: Consumable: offers two effects; you take one now and the other becomes available next show
option_c: Consumable: offers three effects and you take one, with the rejected two raising the odds of better offers later

name: Bus Driver
one_line_summary: Usually great, sometimes awful
option_a: A large multiplier three times in four, and an equally large penalty the fourth
option_b: A large multiplier three times in four, and nothing the fourth
option_c: A large multiplier three times in four and a penalty the fourth, with the odds improving each time it pays out

name: Chocolate Die
one_line_summary: A die decides what happens next
option_a: Beating a boss rolls a die to start a random event
option_b: Beating a boss rolls a die to start a random event, and you may reroll once
option_c: Beating a boss rolls a die whose faces you have collected over the run

name: Color-wheel booth
one_line_summary: Bet on a colour
option_a: Stake a gold card on a suit at a wheel; hitting it pays out several times over
option_b: Stake any number of gold cards on a suit at a wheel; hitting it pays out several times over
option_c: Stake a gold card on a suit; hitting it pays out, and missing converts the stake into a debuff card

name: Glitched
one_line_summary: Every number on it is a lie
option_a: Every value on this card is randomised within a wide band, rerolled each show
option_b: Every value on this card is randomised once, when acquired, and fixed thereafter
option_c: Every value is randomised each act, so the same card is different every time it fires

name: Misprint
one_line_summary: A wildly variable bonus
option_a: Scores a random multiplier between nothing and a large amount, rerolled every act
option_b: Scores a random multiplier between nothing and a large amount, fixed for the whole show once rolled
option_c: Scores a random multiplier, and you may reroll it once per act

name: Run the monte (thrower)
one_line_summary: Run the game yourself
option_a: Play the swindler's side for gold, at the risk of the town's reputation
option_b: Play the swindler's side for gold; being caught bars you from that town for the rest of the run
option_c: Play the swindler's side for gold, with the payout and the risk both set by how long you keep going

name: Snake Oil
one_line_summary: Consumable: gives +3 rank to one card this show, with a seeded 1-in-4 chance of doing nothing
option_a: Consumable: +3 rank to one card this show, with a 1-in-4 chance of doing nothing at all
option_b: Consumable: +3 rank to one card permanently, with a 1-in-2 chance of doing nothing at all
option_c: Consumable: +3 rank to one card this show; on the 1-in-4 failure it instead loses 3 rank

name: The Faro Bank
one_line_summary: A crooked bank
option_a: Gambling node where the house cheats, and you may cheat back
option_b: Gambling node where the house cheats; catching it out pays the whole bank
option_c: Gambling node where the house cheats and you may cheat back, with being caught costing town reputation

name: Trick-or-Treat
one_line_summary: Sold, it is a treat or a trick
option_a: When sold, usually creates two useful tokens, and occasionally a cursed card instead
option_b: When sold, creates two useful tokens or a cursed card at even odds
option_c: When sold, creates tokens or a curse, and you may pay gold to improve the odds

name: Wheel of Death roulette
one_line_summary: A wheel that lands where the knife did
option_a: A bonus wheel spins and pays out on the cell where the last Knives card scored
option_b: A bonus wheel spins and pays out on a random cell, with the payout scaling with that cell's rank
option_c: A bonus wheel spins where the last Knives card scored, and you may re-spin once at the cost of half the payout

name: Fragile
one_line_summary: Its odds cannot be improved
option_a: A large multiplier with a small chance of destruction each trigger, and no effect may alter those odds
option_b: A large multiplier with a small chance of destruction, and odds-improving effects work on it normally
option_c: A large multiplier whose destruction odds cannot be altered, and which grows each time it survives

name: Non Verisimile
one_line_summary: Long odds pay proportionally
option_a: Whenever a probability check succeeds, gains a multiplier equal to how unlikely it was
option_b: Whenever a probability check succeeds, gains a fixed multiplier regardless of the odds
option_c: Whenever a probability check succeeds, gains a multiplier equal to its odds, and loses one when a check fails

name: Oops! All 6s
one_line_summary: Doubles every chance in the game
option_a: Every stated probability in the game is doubled
option_b: Every stated probability affecting your own cards is doubled
option_c: Every stated probability is doubled, including the ones that work against you

name: Wheel of Hope
one_line_summary: Paid for its failures
option_a: Gains a permanent multiplier every time one of your probability checks fails
option_b: Gains a permanent multiplier every time a probability check fails, and loses it when one succeeds
option_c: Gains a permanent multiplier per failed check, scaling with how likely that check was to succeed

name: Injury stacking status
one_line_summary: Injuries stack, and they end careers
option_a: Each act a card performs may add an injury stack, and each stack raises the chance it retires permanently; a card that sits out an act sheds one
option_b: Each act may add an injury stack raising the retirement chance; stacks never clear
option_c: Each act may add an injury stack; a card sits out to shed one, and a protective card lowers the chance

name: Net card lowers retirement, raises injury
one_line_summary: A net changes the odds
option_a: Raises the chance of injury but lowers the chance of retirement
option_b: Lowers the chance of retirement without affecting injury at all
option_c: Raises injury chance and lowers retirement chance, and converts each prevented retirement into fame

name: Contract Ink
one_line_summary: Scores +X points per show it is played; if benched two shows in a row, it is permanently removed from the deck
option_a: Scores bonus points each show it is played; two consecutive shows unplaced and it is removed from the deck for good
option_b: Scores bonus points each show it is played; one show unplaced and it drops a rarity tier
option_c: Scores double points each show it is played, and is removed from the deck for good after five shows regardless

name: Railroad Jump
one_line_summary: Map-edge hazard: traveling this route costs one card, permanently removed from the deck
option_a: Map hazard: taking this route costs one card, removed from the deck for good
option_b: Map hazard: taking this route costs one card of your choice, removed from the deck for good
option_c: Map hazard: taking this route costs one random card, which returns two towns later

name: Bull-leap vault
one_line_summary: Dodges the attack and takes a bow
option_a: When a boss attacks this card's column, it dodges and scores instead
option_b: When a boss attacks anywhere on its grid, this card dodges the hit for the whole column and scores
option_c: When a boss attacks this card's column, it dodges and scores; each successful dodge raises the score it takes

name: Deus ex Machina
one_line_summary: Consumable, once per run: when a show is lost, it is instead won at exactly the goal
option_a: Consumable, once per run: a lost show is instead won at exactly its goal
option_b: Consumable: a lost show is replayed from the start with the same deck and a fresh seed
option_c: Consumable, once per run: a lost show is won, and the next show's goal doubles

name: Press Bribery
one_line_summary: Once: on failing a town, keep touring as if it were won; if still unspent by the final town, converts to an automatic win there
option_a: Once: a failed town is treated as won and the tour continues; unspent at the final town, it becomes an automatic win there
option_b: Once: a failed town is treated as won and the tour continues; unspent, it is simply wasted
option_c: Once: a failed town is replayed with the Entrance order known in advance

name: The Elimination Save
one_line_summary: Two would die, so they duel
option_a: When two cards would be destroyed at once, they duel and the winner survives
option_b: When two cards would be destroyed at once, you choose which survives
option_c: When two cards would be destroyed at once they duel, and the survivor takes the loser's rank

name: The Mime
one_line_summary: Takes the hit for the stack
option_a: Attaches to a stack and absorbs the first hostile effect aimed at any card in it
option_b: Attaches to a stack and absorbs every hostile effect aimed at it, breaking after three
option_c: Attaches to a stack and absorbs the first hostile effect each show, refreshing between shows

name: The Rodeo Clown
one_line_summary: Steps in front of the hit
option_a: Once per turn, when a boss or town effect targets another of your cards, it hits this one instead
option_b: Whenever a boss or town effect targets another of your cards, it hits this one instead, until this card is destroyed
option_c: Once per turn, redirect a hostile effect onto this card, and this card scores bonus points for taking it

name: All In card
one_line_summary: Double now, double the goal
option_a: On the next score, the total doubles, and so does the score needed next round
option_b: On the next score the total doubles, and the next round's goal rises by half
option_c: You choose the multiplier; the goal rises by the same multiplier

name: Flesh Panopticon
one_line_summary: An enormous boss that pays enormously
option_a: Boss: the goal is many times larger than normal, and beating it grants an outsized reward
option_b: Boss: the goal is many times larger, and you may decline it for a lesser reward
option_c: Boss: you set the multiplier on the goal yourself, and the reward scales with it

name: Risk/reward doubled-points tricks
one_line_summary: Bigger tricks fail more often
option_a: Higher-tier tricks pay more and fail more often, with risk-lowering cards to manage it
option_b: Higher-tier tricks pay more and fail more often, and you opt in per trick

option_b: Triples score, with a 1-in-100 chance of being destroyed at the end of each show

name: Cherry Pie

option_b: Take a debuff card for this show in exchange for gold scaling with how bad the debuff is

option_b: Show variant: play the debuffed cards; each one scored clears its debuff permanently

name: Monopoly Money

option_a: A chance that purchases are destroyed on buying, and selling this card halves your gold
option_b: A chance that purchases are destroyed on buying, and selling this card costs all your gold

name: The Dirty Opening

option_b: Grants exactly what its text says, and the text is written to be misread

name: White Elephant

option_b: When a show begins, destroys an adjacent card and permanently gains that card's value

option_b: When a show begins, gains a multiplier and destroys one of your other cards, chosen by you

name: The Ninot

name: No Two Alike
one_line_summary: Repeated actions stop repeating

option_b: Once this fires, no repeated action repeats for the rest of the run

name: The Marked Seed

name: The Prepared Deck
one_line_summary: Makes an outcome stop being random

option_b: Difficulty: one fewer shop slot and one fewer pack slot
option_c: Difficulty: one fewer shop slot, and the slot returns if you win a show without buying anything

name: Ascensions
one_line_summary: Difficulty you opt into
option_a: Each ascension adds one negative card of your choice into the deck or the rules deck
option_b: Each ascension adds one negative card chosen at random into the rules deck
option_c: Each ascension adds one negative card you choose, and one positive card chosen at random

name: Black Stake
one_line_summary: Cards that cannot be sold
option_a: A proportion of cards offered arrive permanently unsellable and indestructible
option_b: A proportion of cards offered arrive unsellable, and the proportion rises with the difficulty level
option_c: A proportion arrive unsellable, and each one you accept lowers the show's goal

name: Brown Stake
one_line_summary: Stickers can stack
option_a: Difficulty: every card sticker may coexist with every other, so one card can carry several drawbacks
option_b: Difficulty: stickers may coexist, but a card carrying two sells for double
option_c: Difficulty: stickers may coexist, and a card carrying three becomes Legendary

name: Diamond Stake
one_line_summary: The tour is longer
option_a: Difficulty: the run must go further before it can be won
option_b: Difficulty: the run must go further, and the extra towns are all bosses
option_c: Difficulty: the run must go further, and you choose how much further for a proportional reward

name: Glass Stake
one_line_summary: Cards shatter as they score
option_a: Difficulty: a small proportion of cards shatter when they score
option_b: Difficulty: a small proportion shatter when they score, and shattered cards pay gold
option_c: Difficulty: a small proportion shatter when they score, rising as the tour goes on

name: Horizon Stake
one_line_summary: The deck keeps growing
option_a: Difficulty: a random card is added to the deck at each show's start
option_b: Difficulty: a random card is added at each show's start, and you may remove one for gold
option_c: Difficulty: a random card is added each show, chosen from cards you have already rejected

name: Platinum Stake
one_line_summary: Fewer shows per tier
option_a: Difficulty: the small shows are removed, leaving fewer chances to earn per tier
option_b: Difficulty: the small shows are removed, and the remaining ones pay more
option_c: Difficulty: one show per tier is removed, and you choose which

name: Purple Stake
one_line_summary: The goal climbs faster
option_a: The score needed scales up faster with each town
option_b: The score needed scales up faster, and the reward scales with it
option_c: The score needed scales faster, and you may spend fame to flatten the curve for one town

name: Dynasty save bonus
one_line_summary: A bonus for finishing again
option_a: A standing bonus for consecutive finished tours in one save file
option_b: A standing bonus for consecutive finished tours, reset by any failed run
option_c: A standing bonus per finished tour, which never resets but grows more slowly each time

name: Seasonal crown
one_line_summary: A title held until someone takes it
option_a: A per-season champion title carried between runs until beaten
option_b: A per-season champion title that grants a standing bonus while held
option_c: A per-season title that grants a bonus while held, and the bonus grows the longer you hold it

name: The Birdman Race
one_line_summary: First to claim it holds it
option_a: A seasonal first-to-claim contest whose winning card holds a title for the whole tour
option_b: A seasonal contest whose winning card holds a title granting a standing bonus until another card takes it
option_c: A seasonal contest that can be re-contested at any town, with the title changing hands

name: The Ghost Show
one_line_summary: Only findable at the right hour
option_a: A secret card findable only in the menu after real-world midnight
option_b: A secret card findable only at a specific real-world hour, differing per profile
option_c: A secret card findable only under a real-world condition the game never states

name: The Rope Trick
one_line_summary: Only real once the rumour is true
option_a: Exists only in rumour and can never be drawn until a hidden condition makes it real
option_b: Exists only in rumour until a hidden condition makes it real, at which point it is added to every future run
option_c: Exists only in rumour; each run raises the chance it becomes real, and it stays real once it does

name: The Screwjob
one_line_summary: The rules betray you, once
option_a: Once per profile, a rule card turns on you at the worst moment, legally by its own text
option_b: Once per run, a rule card turns on you at the worst moment
option_c: Once per profile, a rule card turns on you; surviving the show it happens in unlocks a reward

name: Connect 4 mini-mode
one_line_summary: Four in a row
option_a: A Connect-4 minigame mode played with placed cards
option_b: A Connect-4 side objective running alongside normal play, paying a bonus for four of a suit in a line
option_c: A Connect-4 minigame where the town places against you on the same grid

name: Cups and balls minigame
one_line_summary: Find the ball
option_a: A three-card shuffle minigame available in shops and events
option_b: A three-card shuffle minigame in shops and events, where guessing right upgrades the card you find
option_c: A three-card shuffle minigame whose difficulty rises each time you win it, with the reward rising too

name: Fishing minigame card
one_line_summary: Fish a card out of the deck
option_a: Place this card over the deck to play a fishing minigame for a card from it
option_b: Place this card over the deck to fish; the harder the fish, the better the card
option_c: Place this card over the deck to fish, with one attempt per show and a chance of losing the card instead

name: Forbidden-solitaire event mode
one_line_summary: Click cards straight into hand
option_a: Event mode: clicking a card sends it directly to your hand rather than the grid
option_b: Event mode: clicking a card sends it to your hand, and the hand is scored as a single poker hand at the end
option_c: Event mode: clicking a card sends it to your hand, and you may return one per turn to the board

name: Karuta duel
one_line_summary: First to spot it
option_a: A speed-pick minigame where the first correct click takes the reward
option_b: A speed-pick minigame where each correct click is worth more than the last
option_c: A speed-pick minigame where a wrong click costs you the round

name: Mini Metro mode
one_line_summary: Straights become lines on a map
option_a: The ends of straights become stations joined by their straight, and must serve passengers over a number of turns
option_b: The ends of straights become stations; each new straight extends the network, and the network's size is the score
option_c: The ends of straights become stations that must be connected into a single network before the show ends

name: The Arcade
one_line_summary: A node full of small games
option_a: Map node: play solitaire-variant minigames for tickets
option_b: Map node: play solitaire-variant minigames for tickets, with harder variants paying more
option_c: Map node: play a minigame chosen from three, each tied to a different reward type

name: The Box Theater
one_line_summary: A show inside the card
option_a: Cue: run a one-card mini-submit inside this card, scoring it separately
option_b: Cue: run a one-card mini-submit inside this card; the result is added to whichever line scores next
option_c: Cue: run a mini-submit inside this card using the whole Entrance, scoring it separately

name: Collect number cards to progress
one_line_summary: Collect the numbers, then face the faces
option_a: Win by collecting every number card, which unlocks a final stage against the face cards
option_b: Win by collecting every number card of one suit, then facing that suit's face cards
option_c: Win by collecting every number card; face cards cannot be scored until you have

name: Dispute settled by performance
one_line_summary: Settled by performance, not points
option_a: Show variant: a town dispute is settled by performance rather than by score
option_b: Show variant: a town dispute is settled by which side scores the more varied board, not the higher one
option_c: Show variant: a dispute is settled by matching a formation the town names, not by score at all

name: Hard cap on flush win-con plays
one_line_summary: Win by a flush, but only so often
option_a: Alternate win: a single flush wins the show, with a hard cap on how many flushes a run may ever play
option_b: Alternate win: a single flush wins, and the cap falls by one each time you use it
option_c: Alternate win: a flush wins, and the required flush grows longer each time you win that way

name: Judged-category scoring
one_line_summary: Graded in categories, not totals
option_a: Show: formation, suit variety and stamps are graded as separate scored categories rather than one total
option_b: Show: three categories are graded separately, and you must pass two of the three
option_c: Show: three categories are graded separately, and only your weakest category counts

name: The Balance
one_line_summary: Final-tier boss: cannot be beaten by score; win by ending the show with row total and column total within 10% of each other
option_a: Final boss: score cannot beat it; win by ending the show with the row total and the column total within 10% of each other
option_b: Final boss: win by ending the show with the row and column totals within 10% of each other, while still meeting a reduced goal
option_c: Final boss: win by ending with every grid's score within 10% of every other grid's

name: The Demolition Show
one_line_summary: Score by destroying, not by playing
option_a: Show: discarding scores points per card destroyed, and normal play scores nothing
option_b: Show: discarding scores points per card destroyed, alongside normal scoring
option_c: Show: discarding scores per card destroyed, and the goal is a count of cards rather than a score

name: The Exploration Show
one_line_summary: No goal, just things to find
option_a: Show: no score goal at all, only hidden bonuses to find in a pre-built board
option_b: Show: no score goal, only hidden bonuses, and a limited number of turns to find them
option_c: Show: no score goal; the reward is whatever you uncover, and leaving early keeps what you have

name: The Faire
one_line_summary: The audience performs and you judge
option_a: Show: the town performs and your cards judge them, for easy fame
option_b: Show: the town performs and your cards judge them; judging harshly pays more but costs loyalty
option_c: Show: the town performs, and you score by predicting which of their acts will score highest

name: The One Ring card
one_line_summary: Destroy it and you win
option_a: You always know exactly where this card is, and permanently destroying it wins the match
option_b: You always know where it is, and destroying it wins the match, but only in the final show
option_c: You always know where it is; destroying it wins, and every effect in the game tries to protect it

name: Festival mini-contest node
one_line_summary: Win any one of three
provenance: DESIGN_REFERENCES.md §A8 Middle East, Central Asia, Mongolia
option_a: Map node: win any one of three mini-contests - score, formation or speed - for the prize
option_b: Map node: win any one of three mini-contests; winning two takes a larger prize
option_c: Map node: three mini-contests, and you must declare which one you are attempting before seeing your deck

name: Mini-game score-free events
one_line_summary: Some shows are not about score
option_a: Some encounters replace the score goal with a puzzle objective, such as triggering five times
option_b: Some encounters offer both a score goal and a puzzle objective, and either wins
option_c: Some encounters replace the score goal with a puzzle objective drawn from a pool, revealed only on arrival

name: The Masked Audience / One-on-One
one_line_summary: Fame hidden around the board
option_a: Show: fame sources are hidden around the board to be found rather than scored
option_b: Show: fame is hidden around the board, and a single audience token pays outsized fame if performed to alone
option_c: Show: fame is hidden around the board, and each one found reveals a hint to the next

name: The String Figure
one_line_summary: Copy the pattern
option_a: Copy a displayed board pattern with your own cards for a bonus
option_b: Copy a displayed board pattern for a bonus, with a larger pattern shown each time you succeed
option_c: Copy a displayed board pattern, or invent one the town must copy back

name: The Water Torture Cell
one_line_summary: Three locks, one escape
option_a: Arrives locked under three conditions - covered, column unscored, unmoved - one unlocking per turn in order; a full escape pays a large bonus
option_b: Arrives locked under three conditions that unlock in any order as you satisfy them; a full escape pays a large bonus
option_c: Arrives locked under three conditions; each one you break pays a bonus, and breaking all three pays a much larger one

name: Turning the tip
one_line_summary: A hidden objective revealed after the fact
option_a: Convert an audience faction into fame, with a hidden bonus objective revealed only once the show is cleared
option_b: Convert an audience faction into fame, with the bonus objective stated up front
option_c: Convert an audience faction into fame; the hidden objective is revealed after the show, and completing it later pays out retroactively

name: Wordle-style hidden target card
one_line_summary: Guess the card it is thinking of
option_a: Sets a hidden target rank and suit and reports whether the last placed card is wrong, close, or exact; the first correctly placed line wins
option_b: Sets a hidden target and reports only wrong or exact, with no close
option_c: Sets a hidden target and reports wrong, close or exact; each guess narrows the possibilities visibly

name: Quest-chain triggered stage acts
one_line_summary: A story told in the right order
option_a: A quest chain where each stage unlocks only after the previous one's effect has been triggered
option_b: A quest chain where stages may be completed in any order, but completing them in sequence pays a bonus
option_c: A quest chain where each stage names the next only once the previous is done

name: Built-in symmetric PvP mode
one_line_summary: Same deck, same cards, higher score
option_a: PvP: both players start with the same deck and draw the same cards, aiming for the higher score
option_b: PvP: both players share a deck and alternate taking cards from one Entrance
option_c: PvP: both players use the same deck and card order, and each sees the other's board as it builds

name: Crew formation battle / class legalization
one_line_summary: Crew against crew
option_a: A formation battle against a rival crew, decided by whose formation scores higher
option_b: A formation battle against a rival crew, alternating one formation each until someone cannot answer
option_c: A formation battle against a rival crew; winning makes an outlaw class legal in that town for the rest of the run

name: One-upmanship duel (scissors dance)
one_line_summary: Alternating melds until someone falls short
option_a: Duel: you and a rival alternate melds, each having to beat the last; the first to fall short loses the wager
option_b: Duel: you and a rival alternate melds; falling short costs one card rather than the whole wager
option_c: Duel: alternating melds, each having to beat the last, and you set the wager before seeing your opening board

name: The Eating Contest
one_line_summary: An eating contest
option_a: A sanctioned outing where consuming cards race a rival to eat the town's offering fastest
option_b: An eating contest where the winner keeps everything eaten and the loser keeps nothing
option_c: An eating contest where you wager how much your card will eat before it starts

name: The Laughing Duel
one_line_summary: Break the rhythm and you lose
option_a: A pattern-matching duel against a town where breaking rhythm loses the round
option_b: A pattern-matching duel where each round's pattern is longer than the last
option_c: A pattern-matching duel where you set the pattern and the town must follow, alternating who leads

name: The Showdown
one_line_summary: Same town, against a rival
option_a: Play the same town against a rival's score; the winner takes both crowds
option_b: Play the same town against a rival's score; the winner takes both crowds and one of the loser's cards
option_c: Play the same town against a rival, seeing their board as it builds

name: The Tent Challenge
one_line_summary: Called out by name
option_a: A town champion calls out one of your cards for a duel: win for gold, lose a rank
option_b: A town champion calls out one of your cards; you may substitute another at a cost
option_c: A town champion calls out your highest card for a duel, and refusing costs fame

name: The Apprenticeship
one_line_summary: A quest the card sets itself
option_a: Names an objective when acquired, drawn from a pool; finishing it transforms this card into a Rare version of itself
option_b: Names an objective when acquired; finishing it lets you choose one of three permanent rewards
option_c: Names a new objective each time the previous one is finished, escalating, with a permanent reward each time

name: The Commission
one_line_summary: The town sets you a task
option_a: Rule: each town states one objective; completing it during that show grants a permanent run-scoped effect
option_b: Rule: each town states one objective; completing it grants gold rather than a permanent effect
option_c: Rule: each town states one objective, and you may accept it for a permanent reward or decline it for a smaller immediate one

name: The Contract
one_line_summary: A stated objective with a permanent reward
option_a: Names an objective at run start; completing it permanently upgrades this card for the rest of the run
option_b: Names an objective at run start; completing it permanently upgrades every card of its class for the rest of the run
option_c: Names an objective at run start; completing it adds a new card to your deck permanently

name: The Long Game
one_line_summary: An objective that spans the whole tour
option_a: Names one objective at run start that can only be finished late in the tour, and pays enormously when it is
option_b: Names one objective at run start with a partial reward at each town you make progress in
option_c: Names one objective for the whole tour, and abandoning it at any point converts the progress made into fame

name: The Standing Order
one_line_summary: Attaches a quest to any card
option_a: Attach an objective to any card you own; completing it permanently upgrades that card
option_b: Attach an objective to any card; completing it permanently upgrades that card and destroys this stamp
option_c: Attach an objective to any card; completing it upgrades that card, and the stamp then moves to a card of your choosing

name: Overshoot
one_line_summary: Progress past the target is not wasted
option_a: Rule: progress past an objective's target carries into the next objective
option_b: Rule: progress past an objective's target is converted to fame
option_c: Rule: progress past the target raises the reward rather than carrying forward

name: The Progress Report
one_line_summary: Reading progress costs something
option_a: Cue: reveal the exact progress of one hidden objective, at the cost of an act
option_b: Cue: reveal the exact progress of every hidden objective, once per show
option_c: Cue: reveal one hidden objective's progress for free, but doing so raises what it requires

name: The Tally Board
one_line_summary: How a quest shows its progress
option_a: Rule: every active objective shows its exact progress at all times
option_b: Rule: every active objective shows only whether it is close, not how close
option_c: Rule: objectives show exact progress, but only while you are not in the middle of an act

name: The Open Secret
one_line_summary: Hidden objectives exist and are findable
option_a: Rule: a pool of hidden objectives is live every run; completing one reveals it and pays permanently
option_b: Rule: a pool of hidden objectives is live, and completing one reveals it permanently for all future runs
option_c: Rule: hidden objectives are live, and any you complete stay hidden until the run ends

name: The Retroactive Clause
one_line_summary: Pays for what you already did
option_a: When acquired, checks what you have already done this run and immediately pays out any objective already met
option_b: When acquired, names an objective and counts progress made before you had it
option_c: When acquired, pays out for the single most impressive thing you have already done this run

name: The Unspoken Brief
one_line_summary: A quest you finish before you hear about it
option_a: Carries a hidden objective, announced only once you have completed it, with a permanent reward
option_b: Carries a hidden objective that reveals itself once you are most of the way through it
option_c: Carries a hidden objective, and each show gives you one clue toward what it is

name: The Double Booking
one_line_summary: Two quests that cannot both be finished
option_a: Rule: two objectives run at once and are mutually exclusive; finishing one voids the other
option_b: Rule: two mutually exclusive objectives run at once, and abandoning one early pays a small consolation
option_c: Rule: two mutually exclusive objectives run at once, and you must declare which you are chasing before the second town

name: The Rival Contract
one_line_summary: A quest a rival is also chasing
option_a: Rule: an objective is shared with a rival show; whoever finishes it first takes the reward
option_b: Rule: an objective is shared with a rival, and you can see how far along they are
option_c: Rule: an objective is shared with a rival; finishing second still pays, at a fraction

name: The Ultimatum
one_line_summary: Take the quest or take the payout
option_a: Offers an immediate reward or an objective worth several times more; taking one removes the other
option_b: Offers an immediate reward or an objective; you may take the reward and still attempt the objective at a penalty
option_c: Offers an immediate reward or an objective, and the objective's value rises the longer you leave it unclaimed

name: Maximized
one_line_summary: Only two ranks exist
option_a: Every face card counts as the same rank and every number card as the same rank
option_b: Every card counts as one of two ranks, chosen at run start
option_c: Every card counts as one of two ranks, and which two changes each show

name: Pareidolia
one_line_summary: Everything is a face card
option_a: Every card counts as a face card for every effect
option_b: Every card counts as a face card, and face cards count as no rank at all for runs
option_c: Every card counts as whichever card type an effect is looking for

name: The Backward-Backward
one_line_summary: Cue: reverse the run direction of one column for the rest of the show, so descending counts as ascending and vice versa
option_a: Cue: reverse the run direction of one column for the rest of the show, so descending reads as ascending
option_b: Cue: reverse the run direction of one line for one turn
option_c: Cue: reverse the run direction of every line in one grid for the rest of the show

name: The Blank
one_line_summary: This card has no rank or suit: it can stack on anything and anything can stack on it, but it never melds and scores 0
option_a: Has no rank and no suit: anything stacks on it and it stacks on anything, but it never melds and scores 0
option_b: Has no rank and no suit for stacking, but counts as whatever the line needs when a meld is checked
option_c: Has no rank and no suit, and any line containing it scores as if it had four cards instead of five

name: Wild rank (copycat/understudy)
one_line_summary: Copies whatever it can find
option_a: Rank 0 that also counts as any rank already present in your deck, for stacking and melds; behaves as blank with nothing to copy
option_b: Rank 0 that counts as any rank present on the board, updating as the board changes
option_c: Rank 0 that counts as whichever rank would score its line highest

name: Clowns as wildcard/joker stand-ins
one_line_summary: Clowns stand in for anyone
option_a: Counts as a copy of any other card on the board for meld purposes
option_b: Counts as a copy of any one card on the board, chosen when placed and fixed thereafter
option_c: Counts as a copy of whichever card would complete the best meld in its line

name: Gentleman juggling
one_line_summary: Plain cards become juggling balls
option_a: Skill-less cards in this card's row count as the Balls suit
option_b: Skill-less cards anywhere on this card's grid count as the Balls suit
option_c: Skill-less cards in this card's row count as whichever suit this card is

name: 31/99-style fixed point values
one_line_summary: Odd values, aiming at a total
option_a: Ranks carry fixed odd values - ace 1 or 11, ten worth -10, King worth 99 - and lines score toward a target total
option_b: Ranks carry fixed odd values, and a line scores only if it lands exactly on the target total
option_c: Ranks carry fixed odd values you can see before placing, and overshooting the target scores nothing

name: Freakshow off-rank cards
one_line_summary: No normal number
option_a: Freakshow cards carry no ordinary rank number and cannot be compared numerically
option_b: Freakshow cards carry no ordinary rank, but count as whatever their neighbours need for a run
option_c: Freakshow cards carry a rank outside the normal range, high or low, that no meld can include

name: Half-Step
one_line_summary: This card has rank N and a half, letting it stack legally between rank N and N+1 in runs, but it never participates in poker melds
option_a: This card's rank is N and a half: it stacks legally between N and N+1, but never counts in a poker meld
option_b: This card's rank is N and a half: it stacks between N and N+1, and rounds down for melds
option_c: This card counts as either N or N+1 for any single check, chosen fresh each time

name: Decimal numbers (Half-Step hat)
one_line_summary: Counts as itself and one higher at once
option_a: This card's rank counts as both itself and one higher simultaneously, so it can serve two melds at once
option_b: This card's rank counts as itself and one higher, but only one of the two may score per act
option_c: This card's rank counts as itself, one higher and one lower, serving up to three melds

name: Misrule show
one_line_summary: Ranks upside down
option_a: Show: all ranks are reversed, 2 counting high and King counting low; winning pays large tips
option_b: Show: all ranks are reversed for one act of your choosing, not the whole show
option_c: Show: all ranks are reversed, and you are told which act it will happen in one act ahead

name: The Spin (whirling)
one_line_summary: Its rank turns
provenance: DESIGN_REFERENCES.md §A8 Middle East, Central Asia, Mongolia
option_a: Cycles its rank by one each turn, wrapping from King back to 1
option_b: Cycles its rank by one each turn, and you may stop the cycle once per show
option_c: Cycles its rank each turn, and the cycle speeds up the longer it stays on the board

name: 5 starting suits
one_line_summary: Five suits, not four
option_a: Five suits instead of four, making flushes harder and enabling an anti-flush hand
option_b: Five suits instead of four, with the fifth appearing only via packs
option_c: Five suits, and a line containing all five counts as its own meld

name: Harlequin
one_line_summary: This card counts as both of its printed suits for every comparison, meld, and suit effect, firing both suits' props
option_a: Counts as both of its printed suits for every comparison, meld and suit effect, firing both suits' props
option_b: Counts as both printed suits for melds only; stacking and props use the first
option_c: Counts as both printed suits, and the two swap places each time it scores

name: Ten-suit challenge deck
one_line_summary: Ten suits
option_a: Deck: ten suits instead of four, making flushes far harder and suit variety far easier
option_b: Deck: ten suits, and any five distinct suits in a line counts as its own meld
option_c: Deck: ten suits, of which five are drawn per run so the roster changes

name: The Best Bower
one_line_summary: This card counts as every suit for flush evaluation (but not for suit-stacking rules), and its prop identity is randomly one of the game's props each time
option_a: Counts as every suit for flush evaluation but not for stacking, and its prop is a random one of the game's props each time
option_b: Counts as every suit for both flushes and stacking, and fires no prop of its own
option_c: Counts as every suit for flushes, and fires the prop of whichever suit is most common on its grid

name: Rock Paper Scissors
one_line_summary: Rock, paper, scissors
option_a: At game start becomes rock, paper or scissors; stacking on another such card requires winning the throw, with ties broken by rank
option_b: At game start becomes rock, paper or scissors; it beats one suit and loses to another, and ties never stack
option_c: It re-rolls its throw every time it is placed, so its stacking legality changes each time

name: Clever Hans
one_line_summary: Counts as a copy of its highest orthogonally-adjacent neighbor's rank; with no neighbors, its rank is 1
option_a: This card's rank equals its highest orthogonally adjacent neighbour's rank, or 1 with no neighbours
option_b: This card's rank equals the sum of its orthogonally adjacent neighbours' ranks, capped at 13
option_c: This card's rank and suit both copy whichever neighbour was placed most recently

name: Hanafuda Reskin
one_line_summary: When a town outlaws a suit, all your cards of that suit count as the suit of the adjacent card for that show
option_a: When a town outlaws a suit, your cards of that suit count as their adjacent card's suit for the show
option_b: When a town outlaws a suit, your cards of that suit count as a suit of your choice for the show
option_c: Your cards always count as the suit of whichever orthogonal neighbour was placed most recently

name: The Turk
one_line_summary: Borrows the rank underneath
option_a: This card's rank is the rank of the card directly beneath it in its stack, or 0 with nothing beneath
option_b: This card's rank is the summed rank of everything beneath it in its stack, capped at 13
option_c: This card's rank is the rank of the card beneath it, and it also inherits that card's suit

name: The Wildcard
one_line_summary: Becomes whatever its row already has
option_a: On every board change, becomes a copy of a rank and suit already present in its row
option_b: On every board change, becomes a copy of whichever rank and suit is most common in its row
option_c: On every board change, becomes whichever rank and suit would score its row highest

name: Wild pip
one_line_summary: A pip that borrows from the board
option_a: Wild pip: takes a rank and suit at random from those present on its row, updating on every board change
option_b: Wild pip: takes a rank and suit at random from those present on its grid, fixed once it is placed
option_c: Wild pip: takes whichever rank and suit appear most in its line, updating on every board change

name: The Abacus
one_line_summary: Adds its neighbours together
option_a: This card's rank is the sum of its orthogonal neighbours' ranks, capped at the deck's highest rank
option_b: This card's rank is the sum of its orthogonal neighbours' ranks, uncapped
option_c: This card's rank is the sum of its neighbours' ranks minus its own printed rank

name: The Difference
one_line_summary: Scores the gap, not the value
option_a: Scores the difference between its own rank and its highest neighbour's
option_b: Scores the difference between the highest and lowest ranks in its line
option_c: Scores the difference between its own rank and its lowest neighbour's, doubled if that difference is exactly one

name: The Doubling Act
one_line_summary: Twice the number, once the card
option_a: This card's rank counts as double its printed value for every check
option_b: This card's rank counts as double for melds only, and normal for stacking
option_c: This card's rank doubles each time it scores, until it exceeds the deck's highest rank and wraps to 1

name: The Halving
one_line_summary: Splits the number in two
option_a: This card's rank counts as half its printed value, rounded down, for every check
option_b: This card's rank counts as half for melds and full for stacking
option_c: This card's rank counts as half, and the other half is given to an adjacent card

name: The Dropped Catch
family: X - Absence, failure and the unplayed
one_line_summary: Paid when a line fails
option_a: Scores a bonus for every line that completes and scores nothing
option_b: Scores a bonus for every line that completes and scores nothing, and the bonus grows each time
option_c: Scores a bonus for every line left incomplete when the show ends

name: The Empty House
family: X - Absence, failure and the unplayed
one_line_summary: Failure is the axis
option_a: Rule: the act's combo counts lines that failed rather than lines that scored
option_b: Rule: the act's combo counts both, so a mixed act pays most
option_c: Rule: an act in which every line failed pays a large flat bonus instead of nothing

name: The Safety Net
family: X - Absence, failure and the unplayed
one_line_summary: Turns a failed line into something
option_a: A line that scores nothing instead pays flat points equal to its highest rank
option_b: A line that scores nothing instead pays flat points and clears itself, freeing the cells
option_c: A line that scores nothing may be re-formed once, and pays double if it scores the second time

name: The Bench
family: X - Absence, failure and the unplayed
one_line_summary: Paid for what never came out
option_a: Scores a bonus per card left in the deck when the show ends
option_b: Scores a bonus per card left in the Entrance when the show ends
option_c: Scores a bonus per card that has never once been placed this run

name: The Cut List
family: X - Absence, failure and the unplayed
one_line_summary: Rewards cards for staying in
option_a: Any card that goes a whole show without being placed gains +1 rank permanently
option_b: Any card that goes a whole show without being placed gains a permanent bonus, lost the moment it is placed
option_c: Any card that goes three consecutive shows unplaced upgrades a rarity tier

name: Understaffed
family: X - Absence, failure and the unplayed
one_line_summary: The unplayed are counted against you
option_a: Rule: cards left in the Entrance at show end each subtract from the final score
option_b: Rule: cards left in the Entrance at show end are destroyed
option_c: Rule: cards left in the Entrance at show end are carried into the next show's Entrance

name: One Short
family: X - Absence, failure and the unplayed
one_line_summary: Almost is a state the board can read
option_a: Rule: a line one card short of a meld is marked, and effects may read that mark
option_b: Rule: a line one card short of a meld scores at a quarter value immediately
option_c: Rule: a line one card short is marked, and completing a marked line pays double

name: The Glancing Blow
family: X - Absence, failure and the unplayed
one_line_summary: A prop that misses is worth more
option_a: Every prop that finishes its path without hitting anything scores a bonus
option_b: Every prop that misses scores a bonus, and this card gains a permanent bonus for each
option_c: Every prop that misses is re-launched once from the opposite edge

name: The Near Thing
family: X - Absence, failure and the unplayed
one_line_summary: Paid for coming close
option_a: Scores a bonus for every line that ends the show exactly one card short of complete
option_b: Scores a bonus for every line one card short, and names which card would have finished it
option_c: Scores a bonus scaling with how close the show's final score came to the goal without reaching it

name: Leave No Trace
family: X - Absence, failure and the unplayed
class_group: X4 - Empty space as a resource
one_line_summary: An empty board is the goal
option_a: Rule: ending a show with an empty board pays an enormous bonus
option_b: Rule: ending a show with an empty board pays a bonus scaling with how many cards passed through it
option_c: Rule: ending a show with fewer than five cards placed pays a bonus scaling inversely with the count

name: The Bare Stage
family: X - Absence, failure and the unplayed
class_group: X4 - Empty space as a resource
one_line_summary: Paid for the cells you did not fill
option_a: Scores a bonus per empty cell on its grid when the show ends
option_b: Scores a bonus per empty cell in its own row and column
option_c: Scores a bonus per empty cell on the whole board, across every grid

name: The Reserved Space
family: X - Absence, failure and the unplayed
class_group: X4 - Empty space as a resource
one_line_summary: Spends emptiness
option_a: Cue: consume three empty cells on a grid to fire a large effect; the cells stay unusable for the show
option_b: Cue: consume three empty cells to fire a large effect; the cells return at the end of the act
option_c: Cue: consume any number of empty cells, with the effect scaling on how many you spend

name: The Dead Air
family: X - Absence, failure and the unplayed
one_line_summary: An act that scores nothing is the trigger
option_a: An act that scores nothing fires this card's effect at full strength
option_b: An act that scores nothing fires this card's effect, and the effect grows with each consecutive scoreless act
option_c: An act that scores nothing fires this card's effect and refunds the act

name: The Patient Crowd
family: X - Absence, failure and the unplayed
one_line_summary: Silence is not always failure
option_a: Rule: a scoreless act does not count against the act limit
option_b: Rule: a scoreless act does not count against the act limit, but does drain patience
option_c: Rule: the first scoreless act of each show is free; every one after costs two acts

name: The Slow Burn
family: X - Absence, failure and the unplayed
one_line_summary: Banks the acts you wasted
option_a: Each scoreless act banks a multiplier that is paid out on the next act that does score
option_b: Each scoreless act banks a multiplier, paid out at show end whether or not anything scores after
option_c: Each scoreless act banks a multiplier, and the bank is lost if two scoring acts pass without spending it

name: The Honk
one_line_summary: No mechanical consequence at all
option_a: Cue for a noise and nothing else, unlimited uses, with no effect on play whatsoever
option_b: Cue for a noise; every fifth honk in a show pays a token bonus
option_c: Cue for a noise, and honking on the exact turn a line completes pays a hidden bonus

name: The House Band
one_line_summary: Changes the show, not the score
option_a: While on the board, the music and background change, with no mechanical effect
option_b: While on the board, the music and background change, and the change signals which hazard is coming
option_c: While on the board, the presentation changes and the change is different per class of card that scored last
